sentences.text: In nineteen ninety-four, a store camera photographed a killer.
Police let their suspect go.
The man on the tape looked too tall.
April fourth, around midnight.
Two clerks are closing a Blockbuster Video in Dallas.
Brad Lindsey, twenty. James Armstrong, twenty-six.
An eighteen-year-old walks in with a pistol,
and marches them to the safe in the back office.
It's on a time lock. Nothing will open it tonight.
James runs for the door.
He doesn't make it.
Then the gunman turns to Brad, the only witness.
He leaves with three hundred and ninety-two dollars.
Weeks later, a tip leads police to Leon Dorsey.
But the man in the photos seems taller. They let him go.
Five months later, he kills again, and this time he's caught.
In nineteen ninety-eight, the FBI measures the old tapes.
The man in the doorway is Leon Dorsey's height.
In two thousand eight, Texas executes him.
Brad and James's parents watch through the glass.
